sections.html:
Fort Collins sits in Larimer County, roughly 60 miles north of Denver, and ranks fourth in size among Colorado cities. The 2020 census recorded 169,810 residents, and the latest estimate for 2024 is 170,924. The housing mix is wide: older houses near Old Town, then newer subdivisions that spread south through the late twentieth century.

Owners who sell here are long-time residents, landlords and heirs. What works best depends on the shape the house is in and how soon you have to be gone. A house along College Avenue or near a MAX stop attracts different buyers and renters than one in an outer neighborhood, so mention its location when you describe it. Colorado State University employs more people than anyone else in town, which supports demand around campus.

Payment optionDue date
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Payment in fullApril 30

The county bills on this calendar every year. If February 28 falls on a weekend, ask the treasurer whether the following Monday still counts as on time. Do not assume it does.

Online payment works with a credit or debit card, or with an electronic check that carries no fee. A paper check goes to the Larimer County Treasurer, P.O. Box 2336, Fort Collins, CO 80522. The counter at 200 W. Oak St. is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone line is (970) 498-7020.

Interest builds on late payments, as Colorado law provides. Owners with an escrow account should ask the mortgage servicer for the payoff and for details on any refund of the escrow balance.

Unpaid taxes do not kill a sale. They get cleared at the closing table, and the sequence is short.

  • Phone the treasurer at (970) 498-7020 and ask what the parcel owes.
  • Give that number to your title company, which orders the tax certificate and prints the figure on the closing statement.
  • The money comes out of your proceeds, so nothing has to be paid up front.
  • The title company also works out the share of the year's tax that belongs to you and the share that belongs to the buyer.

A mortgage works the same way. The lender is paid from the proceeds, so get a written payoff statement from your servicer that stays good through the closing date you have in mind.

sections.h2: Registering a rental before you sell
sections.html:
Most long-term rentals in the city, which means homes let for 30 days or more, have had to register every year since January 1, 2025. Owners also certify that the unit meets minimum housing standards.

Registration shapes a sale in a few ways:

  • A buyer planning to keep your tenants will want proof that the registration is up to date.
  • The Rental Housing program gives grants for landlord repairs, with funding rounds typically opening in December for the following year.
  • The program's office is at 281 N College Ave, phone 970-416-2305, email rentalhousing@fortcollins.gov.

Tenants in place do not rule out a sale. Investors often buy occupied houses, and a direct sale suits an owner who would rather not vacate the unit or finish deferred repairs first.

sections.h2: Is your house in a flood zone?
sections.html:
In July 1997 a flash flood killed five people and badly damaged city property and the Colorado State University campus. Buyers remember it. A house near the Cache la Poudre River or a drainage channel will draw a flood zone question, and a lender will ask for the official determination. Check your address on the city's maps ahead of time so you can answer.

A cash buyer weighs the same risk, but no lender requirement for a flood determination sits between the offer and the closing.

When a deed is recorded, the clerk and recorder collects Colorado's documentary fee: one cent on each $100 of the price, rounded up for any leftover part of a hundred. A deal at $500 or under pays nothing. Who covers the fee is a term you settle in the contract.

sections.h2: How a direct sale of a Fort Collins house works
sections.html:
Selling directly drops the listing routine, and you can step out whenever you like.

  • Share the address, the house's condition and your preferred closing date.
  • The buyer studies those details and may visit in person.
  • You receive an offer and decide yes or no.
  • A title company confirms ownership, requests the tax certificate and drafts the closing papers.
  • At the signing you hand over the deed, the Larimer County clerk and recorder records it, and you collect your money.

With cash on the buyer's side, no appraisal or loan approval slows things down. Timing comes down to the title work and your own schedule, so a quick close and a slower one are both possible.

A bit of prep saves days. Find your latest property tax statement, any mortgage payoff figures, and receipts or permits for past repairs. Landlords should add the lease and the city registration details, and tell the buyer whether the tenants intend to stay.

At the walkthrough, point out whatever needs fixing. A cash offer prices the house as it stands today, so you avoid contractor bids, lender-ordered inspections and open houses. Turning the offer down costs you nothing.

On closing day, the title company reviews the final numbers with you before you sign. Taxes, any mortgage payoff and recording charges come out first, and the remainder is paid to you.

Listing a house means cleaning, staging, photographs, strangers walking through on weekends, haggling after the inspection, and weeks of waiting on the buyer's bank. Any of those steps can sink a deal at the last minute. Paying cash cuts out most of the list, and your closing never depends on someone else's loan.

You pay for that convenience in the price. Someone who absorbs the repairs and closes quickly will bid below what a polished house could fetch on the open market. Set the gap against what waiting costs you: another tax installment, utility bills, and the hassle of looking after an empty or tenant-filled house.

sections.h2: Who tends to choose a direct sale
sections.html: Callers here tend to be heirs left with a house they never planned to own, landlords done with a rental, people relocating for work, and owners whose property needs more repair than their budget allows. If you recognize yourself, ask for an offer and hold it up beside a realistic listing estimate after repairs and fees. Pick whichever fits your calendar.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fort Collins rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. An occupied rental can be sold, and an investor may keep the tenants. If the property is registered under the city's 2025 rental program, confirm the registration is current before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Fort Collins house before selling?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers purchase as-is and set the offer with repairs in mind. You skip contractor bids, lender inspections and showings.

faqs.q: When is the Larimer County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and payment in full April 30. Call the treasurer to confirm this year's dates.

faqs.q: Is Fort Collins in a flood area?
faqs.a: Some parcels sit near the Cache la Poudre River and drainage channels, and the 1997 flash flood killed five people. Buyers often check the flood zone, so look up your address on the city's maps.

faqs.q: What is the Colorado deed fee on a home sale?
faqs.a: It is one cent per $100 of the price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when the deed is recorded. The sales contract says who pays.
